Stop babysitting your AI coding assistant. 🛑

Most AI coding agents lack structure, forget context, and skip tests. ECC (affaan-m/ECC) turns AI coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor into disciplined software engineers by adding a structured, self-improving agent harness operating system.

It solves the unreliability of native AI agents by introducing a formalized engineering lifecycle: planning before building, test verification, context-isolated self-review, persistent memory, and continuous learning that turns successful patterns into reusable skills.

What makes it a game-changer for your workflow:

🛠️ Comprehensive Tooling Library: Includes 68 specialized agents, 293 reusable skills, and 94 command shims covering everything from TDD and security reviews to frontend architecture and machine learning workflows.

⚡ Multi-Harness Architecture: Native support and deep optimization for Claude Code and Codex, with capability-limited adapters for Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini, Zed, and GitHub Copilot.

🧠 Runtime Hooks and Memory: Enforces workflow guardrails, generates session summaries, manages persistent cross-session memory, and facilitates continuous learning without bloating the context window.

🛡️ AgentShield Security: Built-in security scanning and validation capabilities to protect development workflows against prompt injection and unsafe agent behavior.

Whether you want to enforce strict TDD workflows before committing or maintain architectural context across long-running sessions, ECC automates the guardrails so you get reliable, production-ready code every time.

Check out the repo and upgrade your AI workflow today:
https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC

🎨 What if Adobe Illustrator was rewritten from scratch in pure, lightning-fast Rust with native AI agent support?

Meet VectorCraft—an ambitious, clean-room reimplementation of professional vector graphics workflows designed to break the mold of bloated, resource-heavy design suites and closed ecosystems. 

🔥 Why developers and engineers are talking about it:
• Blazing Performance: Multithreaded SIMD rendering off the UI thread handles 20,000 shapes in ~27ms at retina resolution while keeping your UI locked at a buttery 120 fps using wgpu.
• Write Once, Run Everywhere: Compiles natively for macOS, Windows, Linux, and FreeBSD, plus runs directly in the browser via WebAssembly from a single shared codebase.
• Agent-Native Architecture: Exposes every menu item, tool gesture, and panel over a JSON control channel and a built-in MCP server. Let LLMs like Claude programmatically draw, edit, and export artwork!
• Advanced Geometry & Storage: Features exact curve booleans, unlimited undo via structural sharing, and native support for .vectorcraft, SVG, and PDF/AI imports and exports.

Whether you are looking for a stellar architectural reference for high-performance GPU-accelerated desktop and web apps in Rust, or you want a blueprint for exposing heavy desktop software functionality to autonomous AI agents, VectorCraft is a must-watch repo.

👉 Check it out on GitHub: https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft

The impossible is happening: Bloodborne is running natively on PC hardware, and it is a masterclass in low-level engineering. 🎮🔥

For years, the dream of playing this masterpiece on PC meant wrestling with heavy hardware CPU emulation. But what if you could skip full emulation entirely and run the original x86-64 executable directly on PC? 

That is exactly what deadinside28/bloodborne_pc achieves by combining an offline binary converter for the PS4 eboot, a targeted runtime implementation for system libraries, and an advanced Vulkan graphics translation layer derived from shadPS4. 

Here is why low-level engineers, graphics programmers, and Linux gaming enthusiasts are calling this a technical triumph:

⚙️ Native CPU Execution: By using an offline-converted memory image and a custom runtime to replace PS4 system libraries, it completely avoids per-instruction CPU emulation overhead.
🧠 Experimental Memory & Translation Model: Maps game memory directly into host system RAM and translates GPU command processing into native Vulkan commands.
⚡ Integrated Temporal Upscaling: Features self-computed motion vectors supporting FSR 3.1, FSR 4, and FSR 4.1.1 with minimal frame-generation overhead.
🧵 Multi-Threaded GPU Processing: Separates command decoding and draw recording to effortlessly scale across modern multi-core hardware.

Whether you want to study advanced Vulkan translation techniques, explore custom memory mapping that minimizes VRAM synchronization, or just see the architecture in action, this codebase is an incredible learning resource.

Check out the repository and dive into the source code here:
https://github.com/deadinside28/bloodborne_pc

Stop settling for generic AI-generated frontend code by giving your AI agent a structured UI design skill that forces radical creative direction, side-by-side visual comparisons, and rigorous iterative refinement.

We have all been there: you ask an AI coding assistant to build a frontend, and you get back the same bland, predictable component layout that requires hours of manual tweaking. 

oil-ui is a specialized AI agent skill that solves this exact bottleneck. Instead of spitting out a single mediocre output, it forces your agent to think like a senior product designer—analyzing your product category, setting a cohesive tone, and generating genuinely distinct stylistic directions.

Here is what makes it a game-changer for your workflow:

✨ Multi-Directional Concept Generation: Automatically creates multiple unique design directions where layout, typography, color palettes, and visual styles significantly diverge.

🖥️ Interactive Proof & Comparison Page: Renders different design concepts side-by-side in a dedicated preview interface supporting desktop and mobile viewports, making it easy to select your favorite.

🔍 Rigorous Evaluation & Refinement: Employs strict visual standards, automated screenshot analysis, and design critiques to clean up clutter and establish a clear focal point.

⚡ Seamless Agent Integration: Installs instantly into supported AI coding agents via npx or direct skill prompts with zero complex configuration required.

Stop wasting time prompting back and forth just to fix layout bugs and uninspired UI. Level up your AI-generated interfaces today!

Want to transform flat web pages into tactile, premium experiences? 

Meet Hairline: a lightweight, zero-dependency micro-interaction library providing twenty-seven isometric line figures that dynamically respond to cursor positioning, clicks, and interactions. 

Frontend developers and UI engineers often struggle to bridge the gap between static layouts and high-end interactive storytelling without bloating their apps with heavy canvas or 3D libraries like Three.js. Hairline solves this by delivering performant vector graphics that operate seamlessly across React and vanilla DOM environments.

Key features you get out of the box:
• Zero-dependency core engine with official React integration and vanilla DOM support (perfect for Svelte, Vue, or plain HTML)
• High-performance animation lifecycle sharing a single requestAnimationFrame loop that pauses automatically when idle or off-screen
• Full accessibility support with ARIA labels, semantic roles, keyboard navigation, and graceful handling of reduced motion preferences
• AI-agent compatibility via an optional skill package that empowers coding assistants like Claude Code and Cursor to autonomously generate custom figures

Whether you are enhancing SaaS landing page hero sections or adding interactive workflow representations to developer dashboards, Hairline saves you hours of implementation time while keeping browser performance optimized. It even respects modern CSS theming variables and integrates smoothly with Tailwind and shadcn.

Check out the repository and start building:
https://github.com/lucasmarkes/hairline
